Raw Client Material:

Discovery call notes, 6 October 2026 (fictional). Attendees: Dana Whitfield,
General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments (fictional); Ravi Okafor, CISO; Ingrid
Solberg, Head of Quality.

- Tamarack designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. HQ in
  the Netherlands; plants in the Netherlands and Germany; sales office in the
  United States. About 1,100 staff; Dana said revenue is "in the US$200 to
  300 million range".
- AI today: a customer service chatbot on the support portal is live
  (deployed). An AI visual inspection system on the German production line is
  in pilot. They plan to use AI for sales forecasting next year.
- Dana: "We are piloting, not scaling. I want governance in place before
  visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."
- Ravi: they run an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS; Ingrid runs the quality management
  system under ISO 9001. They would like to start ISO/IEC 42001 work next
  year.
- Dana named the EU AI Act and the GDPR as the rules they are watching.
- Internal audit reported in June 2026 that there is no inventory of AI
  systems.
- Constraints: budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year; customer
  data must stay in the EU; the German works council must be consulted before
  anything touches production staff.
- Who would attend: Dana, Ravi, Ingrid, the Head of Data (Tomas Reyes), the
  German plant manager and two internal auditors.
- Dana is the budget holder for this. Decision expected by 15 December 2026.

judgment_calls: Part 2 of the fixture is not shown to me. I assumed its INCUMBENT_FRAMEWORKS lists only the ISO 27001 ISMS and ISO 9001 QMS. If it also lists internal audit, this element would pass.

The existence of an internal audit function is arguably entailed by 'Internal audit reported in June 2026', and the field definition includes 'audit programs'. Another scorer could treat it as traceable and pass the case. I applied the v1.14.3 guidance that incumbent functions not stated in the Profile Block are failures, and the fail indicator's 'beyond the framework names'.

I treated 'run by Ingrid Solberg' as supported, since the notes say 'Ingrid runs the quality management system under ISO 9001'. I treated the 'Piloting' maturity as supported by Dana's own statement. The CONFIDENCE_NOTES caveats add no unsupported facts.
score.reasoning: The response meets the format, field-completeness and halt-avoidance checks. It also avoids the main traps: it does not assign an owner to the ISMS, and it does not record an AI inventory or any other register as an incumbent control. It does add 'internal audit function' to INCUMBENT_FRAMEWORKS. That is an incumbent function beyond the framework names, which the scorer guidance and the fourth fail indicator treat as a failure. Because partial compliance is FAIL, the case fails, though this rests on a judgment call about Part 2 that another scorer could decide differently.
